headline: Medium risk: shared file-based workflows can leak or corrupt data, while prompt-injection risk is low because neither agent has a direct shared instruction channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations reads files such as data sources and validation results, while pdf.js reads PDF files; there is no documented direct messaging or shared MCP channel between them. The only plausible bridge is manual file handoff or a shared workspace, so injection is possible but not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory and one agent consumes the other's output as text, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF the operator manually copies PDF-derived text into validation inputs, malicious instructions can be carried across.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Review any copied text before reuse.
Use read-only mounts for PDF inputs.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated validation artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files by default: Great Expectations handles data sources, validation results, and documentation, while pdf.js handles PDF files. Even with no network egress, a shared workspace can expose sensitive document contents or validation outputs across the pair, so leakage is plausible in default file-based workflows.
conditions: IF both agents are granted access to the same workspace, PDF contents can flow into validation artifacts.
IF validation results are stored beside source PDFs, either agent can expose the other's outputs.
mitigations: Separate input and output folders.
Restrict file permissions per agent.
Store validation results outside shared workspaces.
Redact sensitive PDFs before processing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write validation artifacts, while pdf.js supports multiple instances and browser-based tests but has no write or network privileges listed. The overlap is mainly file-based and read-heavy, so direct write conflict is not documented; uncertainty keeps this above none but below medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF package installation is performed in a shared environment, Great Expectations may alter the runtime seen by pdf.js.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Pin dependencies in isolated environments.
Avoid shared mutable caches.
Run pdf.js in a separate worker process.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results and documentation, and pdf.js is a document-processing agent that can consume PDF files. If pdf.js treats Great Expectations outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade from validation artifacts into downstream document handling; the pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF pdf.js ingests Great Expectations-generated reports as source-of-truth text, downstream actions may reflect incorrect assertions.
IF the operator uses validation results to drive document decisions without review, errors propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of validation outputs.
Keep reports separate from source PDFs.
Add checksum checks before reuse.
Mark generated artifacts as non-authoritative.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for downstream inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either open-source agent, and both list no secrets or OAuth scopes. With only docs-level evidence and no compliance divergence shown, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data under a separate policy, compliance review is required.
IF deployment adds third-party logging or retention, the compliance profile changes.
mitigations: Confirm local retention settings.
Avoid regulated data until policies are reviewed.
Document data classes per workspace.
Disable external logging.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
